newsitem.title: INDIA: Cotton-Monsoon revival seen boosting Indian crop.
newsitem.headline: Cotton-Monsoon revival seen boosting Indian crop.

text.p: A revival of monsoon rains ending a two-week dry spell in India has kindled hopes of yet another bumper cotton crop in the 1997/98 (October/September) season, traders said on Thursday.

"As of today, the weather is very good for the cotton crop. If it continues like that for a month, India is certain to harvest yet another bumper crop," said a senior official of the East India Cotton Association (EICA).
EICA has recently estimated the 1996/97 cotton crop at 16.78 million bales (one bale is 170 kg), up from the previous year's 16.27 million.
The four-month June-September monsoon arrived a week late and dried up by the middle of July, causing concern among cotton trade and industry.
Initially, prices looked up on reports of a dry spell in cotton-producing centres, traders said.
"But a revival of the monsoon brought prices down," said Manubhai Amarsey, a leading cotton dealer. India's cotton crop depends mostly on monsoon rains.
Dealers said mills were holding stocks that could last for two to three months and this brought down their buying in the week to Thursday.
"Expectations of a higher new crop for the 1997/1998 season (October/September) also subdued sentiment," Amarsey said. "But it's too early to predict the size of the crop."
Traders said the worst sufferers during the week were short- and medium-staple varieties but long staple cotton remained exceptionally firm.
In spot, Bengal-deshi lost 5.0 rupees to 1,005/1,075 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Punjab saw-ginned shed 5.0 rupees to 1,820/1,855 rupees per maund.

Gujarat Kalyan cotton fell 400 rupees to 14,100/14,700 rupees per candy (355.56 kg), Wagad cotton dropped 100 rupees to 13,000/13,100 rupees and Kala-ginned shed 100 rupees to 12,300/12,400 rupees per candy.
Long-staple cotton remained firm during the week on a shortage of ready stock.
Gujarat Sankar-4 long-staple cotton (average variety) rose 400/500 rupees to 19,000/20,000 rupees per candy . The superior variety made a similar gain at 20,500/21,500 rupees per candy.
